1#main: Which kohen is warned about impurity, for which dead he may become impure, and until when he may become impure. In it are 9 seifim. Just as the kohen is warned not to become impure, so adults are warned regarding minors {Rama: (specifically to make them impure by hands; but if minors impart impurity by themselves, see Orach Chaim siman 343 whether they must be separated) (Rashba siman 128 and Mahariu and Tur in the name of Rambam, who wrote here that separation is not needed).}
2#main: Even a blemished kohen is warned not to become impure; but a challal and kohenet may become impure.
3#main: All the dead mentioned in the parashah for whom a kohen must become impure — it is a mitzvah that he become impure for them, and if he did not wish, they make him impure against his will; whether man or woman.
4#main: These are the relatives for whom he becomes impure: his wife — married and fit; but unfit, or divorced, or betrothed — he neither becomes an onen nor becomes impure for her, and likewise she neither becomes an onen nor becomes impure for him; and he becomes impure for his mother even if she became profaned; and for his son and daughter when it is clear to him that their months were complete, or they are thirty days and onward, even if unfit — except his son and daughter who are mamzer or from a maidservant or gentile woman; and for his brother and sister from his father, even if unfit, unless they are children of a maidservant or gentile woman; but for his brother and sister from his mother he does not become impure; and likewise not for his betrothed sister, even if betrothed to a kohen; and not for one raped or seduced; but he becomes impure for his sister who was betrothed and divorced and is mature, or a woman whose hymen was ruptured by wood; and he becomes impure for a yevamah, even if he wrote in her ketubah: if I die childless your ketubah returns to my father's house (meaning: her father's house).
5#main: All these for whom he becomes impure — even not for need; and some say specifically for need: {Rama: And according to the first view, even if his relative died on Shabbat when he cannot bury him that day, it is permitted to become impure for him and guard him lest he lie in disgrace (Terumat HaDeshen siman 283); and it is proper to be stringent according to the other view — not to become impure except for burial needs and to bring him a coffin and shrouds (there in the name of Tosafot Shanz).}
6#main: He becomes impure for them only until the golel is sealed: {Rama: (And if he intends to move him, it is permitted to become impure for him for need until the second golel is sealed) (responsum of Rashba siman 292).}
7#main: It is forbidden for a kohen to become impure for the dead even while becoming impure for his relatives; therefore a kohen whose relative died must be careful to bury him at the end of the cemetery so he not enter the cemetery and become impure from other graves when burying his dead: {Rama: (Specifically after he left his dead; but while still occupied with his dead, it is permitted to become impure even for others) (Tur).}
8#main: A kohen whose ancestors departed from the community's ways, such as informers (meaning: those who fabricate false accusations), he does not become impure for them; nor for those executed by beit din; nor for one who destroys himself knowingly; nor for a doubt such as when her offspring was mixed with her friend's, or doubt whether a nine-month child of the first or seven-month child of the last.
9#main: A kohen does not become impure for a limb from the living from his father, nor for a bone from his father's bones; and likewise one gathering bones does not become impure for them even though the spine remains — if anything is missing from it, even if placed beside him, he does not become impure for it, for he becomes impure only for a complete one; and some say this is when the deficiency was after death, but if a limb was missing in his lifetime and he died, he becomes impure for him even though not whole: {Rama: (And some say he does not become impure for one executed, for he is called deficient) (Kol Bo in the name of R' Shimon of Aueria); (and it is proper to be stringent).}
